plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 23: Gauss's Law
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional sketch of a small cylindrical Gaussian surface straddling the surface of a charged conductor. The conductor's surface is drawn as a broad, softly shaded lavender sheet receding into the distance, sprinkled with plus signs and labeled 'sigma' at the upper left. A short translucent cyan cylinder stands through the sheet with its axis along the surface normal, one flat end face above the surface and the other below it, and its curved side wall shown in cross-section. The center of the cylinder is marked by a small black dot labeled P lying on the surface itself. A red arrow labeled with a vector E rises from the upper end face along the cylinder axis, and a curved leader from the right names that face 'Delta A'. A second curved leader from the lower left points at the buried portion and labels it 'E = 0'. A bracketed dimension at the left, labeled 'delta', gives the cylinder's height. Setting the outward arrow against the vanishing field below is the point of the drawing: flux crosses only the outer end cap. The construction supports relating the field just outside a conductor in equilibrium to the local surface charge density.

elements: Broad flat conductor surface drawn as a large soft-edged lavender ellipse receding into the distance (the 'infinite' charged sheet), fading toward its rim
Scattered black '+' signs distributed over the sheet representing the uniform surface charge density
Greek label 'σ' placed near the upper-left region of the sheet
Short translucent cyan cylindrical Gaussian pillbox standing with its axis along the surface normal, centered on the sheet, upper half above and lower half below the sheet
Upper flat end cap of the pillbox (the outside cap), drawn as a darker cyan ellipse
Curved side wall of the pillbox shown translucent, with the sheet plane cutting it at mid-height
Lower flat end cap of the pillbox buried below the sheet (drawn faintly / hidden inside the conductor)
Small black dot at the center of the pillbox lying on the sheet, labeled 'P'
Red arrow rising from the center of the upper cap along the cylinder axis (surface normal), labeled with the vector 'E' in bold with arrow overbar
Faint red stub of the same axis line running down through the interior of the pillbox to P
Curved leader line from the right side pointing at the upper cap, labeled 'ΔA'
Curved leader line from the lower left pointing at the buried lower portion of the pillbox, labeled 'E = 0'
Dimension bracket with tick marks on the left side of the pillbox spanning its full height, labeled 'δ'
Dashed normal axis through the pillbox for reference

interactions.teaches: The pillbox truly straddles the conductor surface in three dimensions — half above, half below — rather than sitting on top of it.

interactions.label: Pillbox height δ
interactions.teaches: Shrinking δ shrinks the side-wall area toward zero while the outer cap area ΔA is unchanged, so in the limit the only surviving flux is E·ΔA through the outside cap.

interactions.label: Field region
interactions.teaches: The boundary condition of a conductor in equilibrium: the field just outside is perpendicular to the surface, while everywhere inside the conducting material it vanishes.
Clicking the top cap, side wall, or bottom cap highlights it and shows its flux term (E·ΔA, 0 because E ∥ wall / E = 0, and 0 because E = 0 inside), revealing why σ = ε₀E just outside.

demo_steps.title: The pillbox on the surface
demo_steps.narration: A short cylindrical Gaussian surface straddles the charged conductor surface at point P, its axis along the surface normal.

demo_steps.title: Field just outside
demo_steps.narration: Just outside the conductor the field is perpendicular to the surface, so it pierces only the outer cap of area ΔA, giving flux E·ΔA.

demo_steps.title: Field inside is zero
demo_steps.narration: Inside the conductor in electrostatic equilibrium E = 0, so the buried lower cap and the buried half of the side wall carry no flux.

demo_steps.title: Let δ → 0
demo_steps.narration: Thinning the pillbox drives the side-wall area to zero. Only E·ΔA survives, so E·ΔA = σΔA/ε₀ and E = σ/ε₀ just outside the conductor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: conductor sheet is a flat disc/ellipse in the y=0 plane of radius ~6 units in X and ~3.5 units in Z (rendered as a broad ellipse receding to upper-left/upper-right), soft lavender #e6e4f2 fading to white at the rim with a slightly darker bluish core #d6d5ea. Roughly 25 black '+' glyphs (~0.18 units tall) scattered randomly over the sheet, denser near the center-left; 'σ' label in italic serif at the upper-left of the sheet near (-4, 0.05, -1.5). Pillbox: cylinder radius 0.55, default height δ = 0.7 (slider 0.02–1.2), centered at the origin so exactly half sits above and half below y=0, axis exactly along +Y (surface normal). Cylinder body translucent cyan #a9dfe0 at ~35% opacity with lighter horizontal banding; top cap a more saturated teal ellipse #7fc8c8 at ~70% opacity; bottom cap same teal but dimmed/greyed since it lies inside the conductor. Point P: black dot radius 0.06 at the origin (on the sheet, center of the cylinder), italic 'P' label just right of it. Red E arrow (#d9382f) starts at the top cap center (0, δ/2, 0) and extends 1.3 units straight up along +Y, shaft ~0.05 thick with a cone head; bold 'E' with vector overbar sits at the arrow tip, upper right. A faint red line continues from the top cap down to P inside the translucent cylinder. 'ΔA' label to the right of the cylinder at about (1.6, δ/2 + 0.25, 0) with a curved leader arcing left-down to the rim of the top cap. 'E = 0' label at the lower-left, about (-2.2, -0.9, 0.8), with a curved leader arcing right-up to the buried side wall of the cylinder. δ dimension bracket on the left of the cylinder at x ≈ -0.95, two short horizontal tick arms at y = +δ/2 and y = -δ/2 with inward-pointing arrowheads and italic 'δ' between them. Physics: flux = E·ΔA = σΔA/ε₀ so E = σ/ε₀ directed along the outward normal; side-wall area = 2πrδ → 0 as δ → 0.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the sheet as a circular plane mesh with a radial alpha-gradient texture (opaque center, transparent rim) so it fades exactly like the source; render '+' signs as small sprites or thin crossed boxes lying in the plane so they foreshorten with the perspective view. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transparent:true, depthWrite:false and a modest opacity for the cylinder so the interior red stub and the P dot read through; render the cylinder side wall with side: THREE.DoubleSide. Draw the buried half of the cylinder with a separate darker/lower-opacity material and clip it visually at y=0 by splitting the mesh into two cylinders (above and below) so the slider can scale each half symmetrically. Labels (σ, P, ΔA, E, E = 0, δ) as CSS2D/HTML overlays anchored to world points; curved leaders as QuadraticBezierCurve3 tubes or Line2 fat lines in dark grey. Click picking via Raycaster against three named meshes (topCap, sideWall, bottomCap) — highlight with an emissive tint plus an outline ring and pop a small HTML card with that surface's flux term. When regionView is 'Inside conductor', dim the red arrow and the outside half, and overlay a large 'E = 0' in the buried half; when 'Outside', dim the buried half. Keep the camera framing fixed on orbit so the δ slider visibly changes cylinder height without re-zooming.

authoredContext:
To see this, consider an infinitesimally small Gaussian cylinder that surrounds a point on the surface of the conductor, as in the figure. The cylinder has one end face inside and one end face outside the surface. The height and cross-sectional area of the cylinder are δ and ΔA, respectively. The cylinder’s sides are perpendicular to the surface of the conductor, and its end faces are parallel to the surface. Because the cylinder is infinitesimally small, the charge density σ is essentially constant over the surface enclosed, so the total charge inside the Gaussian cylinder is σΔA. Now E is perpendicular to the surface of the conductor outside the conductor and vanishes within it, because otherwise, the charges would accelerate, and we would not be in equilibrium. Electric flux therefore crosses only the outer end face of the Gaussian surface and may be written as EΔA, since the cylinder is assumed to be small enough that E is approximately constant over that area. From Gauss’ law,

Thus,

An infinitesimally small cylindrical Gaussian surface surrounds point P, which is on the surface of the conductor. The field E→ is perpendicular to the surface of the conductor outside the conductor and vanishes within it.

A surface labeled sigma has plus signs on it. A point P on the surface forms the center of a cylinder. An arrow labeled vector E is along the axis of the cylinder and emerges from its top surface. The top surface of the cylinder is labeled delta A and the bottom surface is labeled vector E equal to zero. These are parallel to the surface sigma. The length of the cylinder is labeled sigma.

For a conductor with a cavity, if we put a charge +q inside the cavity, then the charge separation takes place in the conductor, with −q amount of charge on the inside surface and a +q amount of charge at the outside surface (the figure(a)). For the same conductor with a charge +q outside it, there is no excess charge on the inside surface; both the positive and negative induced charges reside on the outside surface (the figure(b)).

discrepancies: The whole scene is framed very small in the canvas (occupies roughly a third of the viewport width), so the pillbox, bracket, leaders and HTML labels all read as tiny marks — in the source the pillbox and sheet fill the frame and annotations are prominent.
The '+' charges are rendered as very thin, small bars that read as faint smudges/crosses rather than the bold, clearly legible plus signs that dominate the source sheet.

The pillbox reads as a fairly opaque dark-teal solid; the source shows a pale, glassy translucent cylinder with white highlight bands through which the sheet and the red arrow's buried portion are visible.

In the source the red E arrow visibly starts at P inside the pillbox and continues through the top cap; here the interior stub is a barely-visible faint line so the arrow looks like it starts at the cap.

The δ bracket, the ΔA leader and the 'E = 0' leader are drawn much thinner/fainter than the bold hand-drawn arrows in the source, and the δ bracket sits far from the cylinder wall rather than hugging it.
evaluation.notes: Topologically faithful Gaussian-pillbox-at-a-conductor figure with excellent, physics-relevant interactions (δ slider, region toggles, guided steps, clickable faces), but the scene is framed too small and the plus charges, leaders and labels are rendered too faint/tiny to read comfortably compared with the bold source annotation style.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); the issues are purely rendering details — camera framing/scale, glyph boldness, material translucency, and leader/label weight — which are generator-level fixes.

elements: Broad flat conductor surface drawn as a large soft-edged lavender ellipse receding into the distance (the 'infinite' charged sheet), fading toward its rim
Scattered black '+' signs distributed over the sheet representing the uniform surface charge density
Greek label 'σ' placed near the upper-left region of the sheet
Short translucent cyan cylindrical Gaussian pillbox standing with its axis along the surface normal, centered on the sheet, upper half above and lower half below the sheet
Upper flat end cap of the pillbox (the outside cap), drawn as a darker cyan ellipse
Curved side wall of the pillbox shown translucent, with the sheet plane cutting it at mid-height
Lower flat end cap of the pillbox buried below the sheet (drawn faintly / hidden inside the conductor)
Small black dot at the center of the pillbox lying on the sheet, labeled 'P'
Red arrow rising from the center of the upper cap along the cylinder axis (surface normal), labeled with the vector 'E' in bold with arrow overbar
Faint red stub of the same axis line running down through the interior of the pillbox to P
Curved leader line from the right side pointing at the upper cap, labeled 'ΔA'
Curved leader line from the lower left pointing at the buried lower portion of the pillbox, labeled 'E = 0'
Dimension bracket with tick marks on the left side of the pillbox spanning its full height, labeled 'δ'
Dashed normal axis through the pillbox for reference

interactions.teaches: The pillbox truly straddles the conductor surface in three dimensions — half above, half below — rather than sitting on top of it.

interactions.label: Pillbox height δ
interactions.teaches: Shrinking δ shrinks the side-wall area toward zero while the outer cap area ΔA is unchanged, so in the limit the only surviving flux is E·ΔA through the outside cap.

interactions.label: Field region
interactions.teaches: The boundary condition of a conductor in equilibrium: the field just outside is perpendicular to the surface, while everywhere inside the conducting material it vanishes.
Clicking the top cap, side wall, or bottom cap highlights it and shows its flux term (E·ΔA, 0 because E ∥ wall / E = 0, and 0 because E = 0 inside), revealing why σ = ε₀E just outside.

demo_steps.title: The pillbox on the surface
demo_steps.narration: A short cylindrical Gaussian surface straddles the charged conductor surface at point P, its axis along the surface normal.

demo_steps.title: Field just outside
demo_steps.narration: Just outside the conductor the field is perpendicular to the surface, so it pierces only the outer cap of area ΔA, giving flux E·ΔA.

demo_steps.title: Field inside is zero
demo_steps.narration: Inside the conductor in electrostatic equilibrium E = 0, so the buried lower cap and the buried half of the side wall carry no flux.

demo_steps.title: Let δ → 0
demo_steps.narration: Thinning the pillbox drives the side-wall area to zero. Only E·ΔA survives, so E·ΔA = σΔA/ε₀ and E = σ/ε₀ just outside the conductor.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: conductor sheet is a flat disc/ellipse in the y=0 plane of radius ~6 units in X and ~3.5 units in Z (rendered as a broad ellipse receding to upper-left/upper-right), soft lavender #e6e4f2 fading to white at the rim with a slightly darker bluish core #d6d5ea. Roughly 25 black '+' glyphs (~0.18 units tall) scattered randomly over the sheet, denser near the center-left; 'σ' label in italic serif at the upper-left of the sheet near (-4, 0.05, -1.5). Pillbox: cylinder radius 0.55, default height δ = 0.7 (slider 0.02–1.2), centered at the origin so exactly half sits above and half below y=0, axis exactly along +Y (surface normal). Cylinder body translucent cyan #a9dfe0 at ~35% opacity with lighter horizontal banding; top cap a more saturated teal ellipse #7fc8c8 at ~70% opacity; bottom cap same teal but dimmed/greyed since it lies inside the conductor. Point P: black dot radius 0.06 at the origin (on the sheet, center of the cylinder), italic 'P' label just right of it. Red E arrow (#d9382f) starts at the top cap center (0, δ/2, 0) and extends 1.3 units straight up along +Y, shaft ~0.05 thick with a cone head; bold 'E' with vector overbar sits at the arrow tip, upper right. A faint red line continues from the top cap down to P inside the translucent cylinder. 'ΔA' label to the right of the cylinder at about (1.6, δ/2 + 0.25, 0) with a curved leader arcing left-down to the rim of the top cap. 'E = 0' label at the lower-left, about (-2.2, -0.9, 0.8), with a curved leader arcing right-up to the buried side wall of the cylinder. δ dimension bracket on the left of the cylinder at x ≈ -0.95, two short horizontal tick arms at y = +δ/2 and y = -δ/2 with inward-pointing arrowheads and italic 'δ' between them. Physics: flux = E·ΔA = σΔA/ε₀ so E = σ/ε₀ directed along the outward normal; side-wall area = 2πrδ → 0 as δ → 0.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the sheet as a circular plane mesh with a radial alpha-gradient texture (opaque center, transparent rim) so it fades exactly like the source; render '+' signs as small sprites or thin crossed boxes lying in the plane so they foreshorten with the perspective view. Use MeshPhysicalMaterial with transparent:true, depthWrite:false and a modest opacity for the cylinder so the interior red stub and the P dot read through; render the cylinder side wall with side: THREE.DoubleSide. Draw the buried half of the cylinder with a separate darker/lower-opacity material and clip it visually at y=0 by splitting the mesh into two cylinders (above and below) so the slider can scale each half symmetrically. Labels (σ, P, ΔA, E, E = 0, δ) as CSS2D/HTML overlays anchored to world points; curved leaders as QuadraticBezierCurve3 tubes or Line2 fat lines in dark grey. Click picking via Raycaster against three named meshes (topCap, sideWall, bottomCap) — highlight with an emissive tint plus an outline ring and pop a small HTML card with that surface's flux term. When regionView is 'Inside conductor', dim the red arrow and the outside half, and overlay a large 'E = 0' in the buried half; when 'Outside', dim the buried half. Keep the camera framing fixed on orbit so the δ slider visibly changes cylinder height without re-zooming.
